Rugged tablet for Klipboard

Klipboard is field service and job management software built in the UK. It started life as Klipboard Limited, which is still the developer named on its Google Play and App Store listings, and since July 2024 it has been part of Kerridge Commercial Systems Ltd, which now trades as Klipboard and sells it as its Field Service Management product. The vendor describes it as connecting scheduling and dispatch, digital job sheets, job costing, inventory, customer communication, invoicing and payments and accounting integrations in one system, with fire safety, HVAC, water treatment, plumbing, facilities management and healthcare equipment servicing among the sectors its customers come from. The office runs the web dashboard; engineers work from the Klipboard mobile app on iOS and Android.

The mobile app is where the site work happens. The vendor's help centre documents workflow forms that must be completed before a job can be closed, photographs and PDF documents uploaded from the device to the job, asset service records with up to six images and an Add Signature step, and asset QR code tags that are scanned in the app to pull up an asset's details and history. Its App Store listing describes image and electronic signature capture from clients in the field and a live map of team members' GPS positions. The help centre also tells engineers who expect to work where there is little or no data coverage to sync their jobs, forms, documents and assets before they set off, which is the pattern of a device that spends its day in a van, a plant room or a roof space and comes back to signal later.

This page sets out what Klipboard publishes about the devices its app runs on, which Tuga rugged tablets meet those published requirements, where the Windows option fits and where it does not, and how a UK contractor can buy a single trial unit before committing to a fleet.

Requirements

What Klipboard needs from a device

Each item below comes from Klipboard Limited (Kerridge Commercial Systems)'s own listing or documentation, with the source linked.

  • Android 12 or later with at least 4GB RAM

    The vendor's Klipboard iOS & Android Device Requirements article (last updated 31 July 2026) states that Android devices need version 12 or later with at least 4GB RAM, and that iPhone and iPad need iOS 13.0 or later. No storage figure is published. The article adds that the minimums may change over time, recommends keeping the device on the latest software, and warns that untested device models, even ones that meet the minimums, may have issues that are harder to troubleshoot. An old launch announcement for the Android app quoted Android 4.1; the device requirements article is the current figure. Source: intercom.help

  • Android app from Google Play, published by Klipboard Limited

    The Android app is published on Google Play as Klipboard (package com.app.klipboard.phone, developer Klipboard Limited). When checked on 19 October 2026 the listing showed version 54.0.11, updated on 16 October 2025. The listing we fetched did not show a Requires Android figure or a clear phone and tablet device breakdown, so the Android 12 floor comes from the help centre article rather than Google Play. The help centre's Getting Started article says the app is available on iOS and Android and gives mobile users a QR code to download it. Source: play.google.com

  • Sync before going offline, with a data connection needed to sync

    The vendor does not publish a dedicated offline mode article. Instead its mobile app articles say that the Sync Jobs button downloads current job data, including scheduled jobs, assets and inventory, only when the device has a suitable data connection, that the first sync takes longer and the app should be kept open during it, and that team members who expect to work offline or in areas with limited or no data coverage should sync their devices and download the required workflow forms, documents and assets before going to the job. The app warns that any completed jobs not uploaded will be lost on logout, so completed work has to be synced before switching device. How much data is held on the device is not published. Source: intercom.help

  • Asset QR code tags scanned in the app

    The help centre says Klipboard generates a unique QR code tag for each asset, and that on the mobile app a team member can find an asset's details and service records by scanning the asset QR tag or by searching; if the tag is scanned the details are downloaded automatically. A damaged or missing tag can be replaced by tapping Add / Edit QR, which opens the in-app QR scanner, then scanning a pre-printed tag. The articles describe an in-app scanner only; no dedicated hardware scan engine, external scanner or barcode format is documented, so on any device the scan path is the app and its camera. Source: intercom.help

  • Workflow forms, photos, documents and signatures in the app

    The Complete A Job article says mandatory workflow forms must be completed before a job can be completed, that extra forms can be added on the app, that forms must be uploaded to be viewable on the web dashboard, and that PDF documents or photographs can be uploaded from the mobile device to the job. The asset service record article says team members can take up to six images within each service record and select Add Signature before syncing the record to the dashboard. The App Store listing describes capturing images and electronic signatures from clients in the field, with double signatures on forms from version 3.7. The vendor does not publish a camera resolution or screen size requirement. Source: intercom.help

  • GPS live tracking and timers with the app open or in the background

    The GPS Live Tracking & Timer On App article says a team member must have the Klipboard app open or running in the background for their real-time GPS location to be seen from the office, that travel and job time are recorded with Start Travel, Arrived and the in-app timers, that the timer continues even if the team member is not on the app, and that the device needs to be connected to the internet for this data to be shared. No location accuracy or hardware requirement is published. Source: intercom.help

  • Windows: no Windows app, web dashboard in a browser

    Klipboard publishes mobile apps for iOS and Android only, and the vendor's site links office users to the web dashboard at app.klipboard.io. No Windows app is published and the device requirements article covers iOS and Android only. The vendor does not publish a supported browser list or minimum browser versions for the web dashboard; the only browser guidance in the help centre is to keep the browser open during data imports. Treat the web dashboard as a current desktop browser product and check it on your own browser before buying for an office. Source: klipboard.com

Setting up

Getting Klipboard running

  1. Ask your Klipboard administrator to add the engineer as a team member with mobile access on the web dashboard and to set the Team Member App Sync Settings, which control how far ahead scheduled jobs reach the device.
  2. On the Tuga A10, A8 or A6, open Google Play and install Klipboard (package com.app.klipboard.phone, developer Klipboard Limited). Confirm the account from the email Klipboard sends, then sign in; the vendor allows five attempts before the account is disabled from the dashboard, and an optional 4-digit PIN can be added.
  3. Run the first Sync Jobs with the app open and on a stable connection. The vendor says the first sync takes longer than later ones because of the volume of data, and that scheduled jobs, assets and inventory come down together.
  4. Allow camera and location access when prompted so the in-app QR scanner, photo capture and GPS live tracking can work, and let the app run in the background, which the vendor says is needed for real-time location and for the travel and job timers to keep going.
  5. Before the first job in an area with limited or no coverage, sync and download the workflow forms, documents and assets the vendor says to prepare in advance, and use Sync Assets on any job that does not yet show the client's registered assets.
  6. Test the QR scanner against an asset tag already generated in Klipboard, complete a test job with a mandatory workflow form, photos and a service record signature, then upload it and check it arrives on the web dashboard as Pending before rolling out to the team.
  7. Make syncing the end-of-day habit: the app warns that any completed jobs not uploaded will be lost on logout, so completed work must be synced before an engineer switches to another device.
  8. On a Tuga W10, open app.klipboard.io in Edge or Chrome and keep the browser updated. Use it for office work; it will not run the mobile app. For the A10 and A8, fit the vehicle mounting dock in the van; for the A10 and W10, add the charging dock where devices live overnight; for the A6, add the belt holster. Fit the tempered glass screen protector before the device goes out.

Questions

Klipboard on a Tuga device

Klipboard's device requirements article publishes Android 12 or later with at least 4GB RAM. The Tuga A10 runs Android 14 with Google Play and has 8GB RAM and 128GB storage, so it meets each published figure with headroom. The Tuga A8 (Android 12, 6GB RAM) meets the Android figure exactly and the RAM figure with headroom, and the Tuga A6 (Android 15, 4GB RAM) meets the Android figure with headroom and the RAM figure exactly. We do not describe any device as certified or tested by Klipboard; the vendor itself says untested models may be harder to troubleshoot, and these are its published requirements set against the device specifications.

The vendor does not publish a dedicated offline mode article, but its mobile app guides say that team members who expect to work offline or in areas with limited or no data coverage should sync their devices and download the required workflow forms, documents and assets before going to the job, and that syncing itself needs a data connection. Completed jobs have to be uploaded afterwards, and the app warns they are lost if the engineer logs out first. The A10, A8 and A6 all run the Google Play app and have dual SIM 4G, which gives a second network to fall back on for the sync. A Tuga W10 can only use the web dashboard in a browser, and the vendor does not document offline working there.

Klipboard's help centre says every asset gets a unique QR code tag, and that on the app an engineer can pull up an asset's details and service records by scanning the tag or by searching, and can link a replacement tag through the in-app QR scanner. The A10, A8 and A6 all have a 13MP rear camera with flash, and on each of them scanning runs through the camera via the app. The A6 also has a Zebra 2D scan engine, but the vendor documents no dedicated scan engine or external scanner support, so do not buy it for that reason alone.

Both meet Klipboard's published requirements, but the A8 does so with no Android headroom: it runs Android 12 against a minimum of Android 12 or later, and the vendor says its minimums may change over time. The A10 runs Android 14, has more RAM (8GB against 6GB), a sharper 1920 x 1200 screen for multi-screen workflow forms and service records, IP68 against IP67, and MIL-STD-810H, which the A8 does not have. The A8 has a 1000 nit screen against the A10's 350 nits, a removable battery, VESA mount points, and costs £379 against £449. Engineers who mostly work outdoors or do long days away from a charger may prefer the A8; those filling in long forms, working in wetter and harder conditions, or keeping the device for several years are better served by the A10.
